title: Producing and Analysing Free Indirect Discourse

sections.content:
You know how to recognise free indirect speech from B2 Unit 17 (*Ana miró el reloj. ¿Dónde estaba Pedro? Otra vez llegaba tarde.*). At C1, literary analysis moves from recognition to **producing** the shift and explaining its **ironic effect**:

• **Turning direct thought into free indirect discourse**: drop the reporting verb (*pensó que*) and quotation marks, shift the pronoun to 3rd person, shift present → imperfect, preterite/present perfect → pluperfect, and future → conditional, while keeping the character's questions, exclamations, and deictics (*ahora*, *mañana*, *aquí*).
• **Analytical function**: when an omniscient narrator adopts a character's voice without signalling the boundary, the prose reveals whether the character is unreliable or self-deceiving, and small slips delate (*delatan*) the gap between thought and reality.

sections.title: Direct thought -> Free indirect discourse
rows: Pensó: «¿Por qué nadie me cree ahora?»
¿Por qué nadie le creía ahora? (imperfect + ahora)

items.spanish: El protagonista cerró la carta. ¿Cómo había podido confiar en un desconocido?
items.english: The protagonist closed the letter. How could he have trusted a stranger?

items.spanish: En este pasaje, el monólogo interior se funde con la prosa narrativa sin verbo introductorio.
items.english: In this passage, the interior monologue merges with the narrative prose without an introductory verb.

items.spanish: Mañana mismo entregaría las llaves y nadie volvería a hacerle preguntas.
items.english: Tomorrow he would hand over the keys and no one would ask him questions again.

items.spanish: Un narrador poco confiable suele delatar sus propios prejuicios mediante el estilo indirecto libre.
items.english: An unreliable narrator often gives away their own biases through free indirect style.

sections.content: Do not mix a reporting verb (*pensó que*) with free indirect discourse: once you write *pensó que*, you are back in standard reported speech. Equally, keep the verb in a past tense (*estaba*, *había cometido*, *explicaría*): using the present tense (*¿Por qué nadie le cree ahora?*) breaks the past-tense narrative frame.
